elements.element: Renewal occurs only by mutual written agreement or through automatic renewal.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 uses the permitted automatic-renewal route: “Each Order Form renews.”

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 states that each Order Form “renews for twelve months.”

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out by giving 30 days’ notice.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 allows “either Party,” which includes Customer, to prevent renewal by giving 30 days’ advance written notice.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before the renewal date.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence requires Vendor to notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least 60 days before the renewal date.

elements.element: Renewal price increases are capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 caps recurring-Fee increases at the lesser of the preceding 12-month CPI increase and 3%.
Section 8.2 provides that each Order Form renews unless timely notice is given.

elements.element: The advance non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 requires only 30 days’ advance written notice from either Party.

elements.element: Renewal price increases are capped at 5% or less.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 imposes the stricter cap of the lesser of CPI and 3%.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the preferred automatic-renewal route: 12-month renewals, a 30-day Customer opt-out right, a Vendor reminder at least 60 days before renewal, and the existing lesser-of-CPI-and-3% price cap. It also satisfies the fallback. The changes are limited to shortening the original notice period and adding the required reminder, without disturbing unrelated terms.
